newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia labour leader has appendicitis, TB.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia labour leader has appendicitis, TB.

text.p: Independent labour leader Mucthar Pakpahan, facing subversion charges in Indonesia, has had his appendix removed and is suffering from tuberculosis, his wife said on Saturday.
Rosintan Pakpahan told Reuters that her husband had his appendix removed on Friday. He was was admitted to the Cikini private hospital on March 7 suffering from a long-standing ailment of vertigo.
"The operation was successful and he is getting better. He can already walk a bit," Rosintan said.

She said an earlier diagnosis that her husband has a tumor in his right lung appeared to be wrong, but he has begun treatment for tuberculocis. She did not know how much longer he would be hospitalised.
The Brussells-based International Confederation of Free Trade Unions on Friday called on Indonesian President Suharto to authorise Pakpahan to travel abroad for medical treatment.
Pakpahan made a request to be allowed to do so after receiving offers from the United States government and European trade unionists to fund such treatment.
"Officially, the justice minister has not sent a letter to us saying he has refused, but we know from the television and newspapers that he has refused to give permission," Rosintan said.

Pakpahan, head of the unrecognised Indonesian Labour Welfare Union (SBSI), was one of a number of activists arrested and charged with subversion after rioting in the capital Jakarta last July in which at least five people died.
Subversion carries the death penalty in Indonesia.
